summary: RADCOM Ltd. filed a Form 6-K reporting Q2 2026 results and disclosed that its board and management are moving to establish a $20-25 million share repurchase program. The filing includes quarterly financials: revenues of $11.8 million, down 33.4% year-over-year, with $109.7 million in cash and no debt. The buyback program is at an early stage, with no specific price, timeline, or authorization mechanics detailed yet. The company cited timing-related deployment delays rather than demand changes, securing three new contracts post-quarter. What to watch: approval details of the repurchase program, execution pace, and whether the buyback supports the stock price given the revenue decline.
